title: AuroraForge NT100 WWE PC Modding Evidence Library
policy: A demonstration establishes only the result, game version, tool version, files, and conditions visibly shown. Unsupported details remain unknown. Proprietary scripts, add-ons, game assets, and packaged files are never redistributed.

sources.title: Clips Editor!
sources.notes: The public post and its interface screenshot establish announced capabilities and visible controls only. Publication predates the Tribute 26 launch, and no public WWE 2K26 end-to-end demonstration was located.

sources.title: Local Tribute Clips Editor v2.21 inspection recording
sources.notes: Silent 2560x1440 recording. Demonstrates read-only opening, inspection, export dialogs, slice bounds, and Clip Viewer preview against locally extracted WWE 2K26 entrance files. It does not demonstrate a modified save, bake, game registration, or in-game result. Tool provenance is not established by the recording.

sources.title: Local Tribute arena profile, props map, and arena-slot recording
sources.notes: The recording visibly shows Tribute 26 v1.4.1 and CakeView in a WWE 2K26 workflow. Around 00:30-01:00 it opens a Tribute package and arena-profile/props-map folders; around 01:10-01:50 it opens Props Manager, Edit Prop Maps, loads prop assets, and imports an arena-props map; around 02:00-02:30 it opens Add Arena Slot with arena, thumbnail, stage, announcer/commentary, hash, and behavior fields; around 02:30-02:40 it displays a successful new-arena-slot message. It does not prove every field's meaning, universal IDs, final bake output, or an in-game result.

sources.title: Face-paint material parameter repair guidance
sources.notes: The user confirms these tutorial references as verified sources. The demonstrated guidance opens the affected base materials in Material Editor, selects the head, confirms or adds the two face-paint parameters as hashes rather than strings, assigns face-paint color and normal files, saves, rebakes the CAK, and tests in game. Exact parameter labels and build identifiers remain source-specific.

sources.title: User-supplied WWE 2K26 tutorial video folder
sources.notes: The user confirms all supplied recordings as verified tutorial sources. Nine recordings were inventoried: Blender/PWM model and attire work, a Tribute update merge walkthrough, an Animation Editor and Clips Editor workflow, a long custom-move installation walkthrough, and a Blender Material Editor workflow. Individual timestamps are recorded in the facts that rely on this set.

sources.title: Animation Editor and Clips Editor WWE 2K26 walkthrough
sources.notes: The recording visibly shows Animation Editor browsing a WWE 2K26 CAK definition tree and event list, CakeView archive browsing, Clips Editor v2.21.4.7.2791 opening MotionArea .clips files, clip counts and metadata, and Clip Viewer previewing two actors. It does not visibly complete a splice, injection, save, bake, or in-game result.

sources.title: Custom move installation walkthrough
sources.notes: The recording visibly presents a custom-move package and source .wem/.move files, Tribute Move Editor, CakeView archive/bake screens, Animation Editor definition/event editing, WWE 2K26 .clips files, and a staged CAK output. It does not visibly establish that a custom move was successfully used in an in-game match.

sources.title: Tribute update-folder merge walkthrough
sources.notes: The recording visibly shows Tribute 26 v1.3.1, an UPDATE folder, Merge UPDATE Files, and selectable groups including roster, SDB, belts, props, MoveData, movies, arenas/GFX, music, crowd signs, teams/templates, and entrance/victory data. It shows the merge dialog and folder structure, not a complete post-merge rebake or game test.

sources.title: PWM Blender import and Material Editor workflow
sources.notes: The recording visibly shows Blender 5.1.1 importing a Tribute/WWE 2K26 model with shape keys, material textures, attachment points, and HPL options; a textured multi-piece wrestler; and Material Editor Release 1.20.0 targeting WWE 2K26 with MTLS/JMTL dual mode, material rows, and material configuration. It does not show a final export, bake, or in-game validation.

sources.title: Tribute Clips Editor current-version announcement on X
sources.notes: Public post text states that the updated Clips Editor previews game animations such as moves and splices them into new animations, and tags WWE 2K26. The post does not disclose exact splice controls, file paths, registration, bake, or in-game acceptance steps.

limitations: The announcement does not prove complete support for every asset

facts.fact: Tribute's current public announcement says the updated Clips Editor previews game animations such as moves and splices them into new animations for WWE 2K26. The tool's interface exposes clip ID/hash search, FPS, bone, shape-key and keyframe metadata; clip injection/export; frame-bounded slices; rebuild/splice; and a Clip Viewer. A local recording demonstrates v2.21 opening WWE 2K26 entrance file 114.clips, listing 46 records, inspecting metadata, opening export and injection dialogs, defining a frame slice, and previewing selected one- and two-actor clips.
